quote: What makes the film great, or near great, is its hugeness of aspiration. Iñárritu is trying to make the ultimate statement about our time. He can’t possibly succeed completely, but he takes a big swing and makes serious contact.
author: Mick LaSalle

quote: Tom Cruise turns in a career best performance in Oscar winning director Alejandro G. Iñárritu’s brilliantly challenging and risky satire Digger.
author: Karen Gordon

quote: A bold statement made even bolder by the person starring in it — screw jumping off mountains, satirizing the men in charge with this level of viciousness feels like the biggest risk of Tom Cruise's career. But it pays off brilliantly.
author: Liz Shannon Miller

quote: Hilarious, infuriating, confusing, but always powerful, Digger is an audacious swing from both the director and its star. Few will see the twist in the tale coming, and not everyone will like how strange things get. For those who do, this is a wildly inventive adventure that sees Tom Cruise relishing his time outside his comfort zone.
author: Victoria Luxford

quote: The film leaves us with the uneasy possibility that the story can end, the audience can applaud, and the iceberg will simply keep inching towards our collective doom.
author: Rodrigo Perez

quote: Digger is funny, but not necessarily fun. It's a pitch-black comedy with an even darker message that may just knock the wind out of you.
author: Jake Kleinman

quote: The biggest problem with Digger might just be that bold ambition. There are a lot of thematic ideas at play here, even before the big shift. A lesser movie might have buckled under the pressure, with too many concepts bouncing off one another and distracting from the underlying throughline. Instead, this film benefits immensely from a fully committed cast and crew, all coming together behind Iñárritu's direction and the screenplay to deliver something masterful.
author: Brandon Zachary

quote: Rather than being a crowd-pleasing prestige picture, it's a love-it-or-hate-it folly – and there probably will be more people in the "hate it" camp than the "love it" one.
author: Nicholas Barber

quote: Risky art is often called a high-wire act, but Tom Cruise’s latest film really earns the label. Until it took its very last step, I honestly couldn’t have told you whether it was going to come off or splat headfirst into the sawdust.
author: Robbie Collin

quote: It’s uncomfortable, it’s bombastic, but don’t listen to anyone who tells you it isn’t funny.
author: Phil de Semlyen

quote: Digger suffers from being too smart for its own good and lacking emotional resonance. As a thought experiment and a love/hate letter to our desire to impose narrative and memorialise reality, though, it’s fascinating.
author: Rosie Fletcher

quote: Iñárritu’s grand black comedy initially seems like a modern Dr. Strangelove—a bleak satire of the end of the world caused by not atomic but environmental catastrophe. But it doesn’t take long for the filmmaker to reveal his conceit.
author: David Sims

quote: But, like the film, it’s the quieter, foreboding moments of [Cruise's] performance that stick with you.
author: Jake Coyle

quote: Wearing facial prosthetics, a faux beer belly and a Texas-sized twang, Cruise pushes his own considerable boundaries and reminds that the dude can still put on an acting masterclass when he wants.
author: Brian Truitt

quote: In terms of real-life figures, Digger is an unholy blend of oil barons, Big Tech CEOs, and the current administration. "Digger" is not a comfortable film by any means, which makes it hard to love.
author: Bill Bria

quote: Seldom have I encountered a greater disjunction between the bludgeoning overkill of a film’s verbiage and the playful sublimity of its visuals. Iñárritu’s technique transcends gimmickry.
author: Justin Chang

quote: It takes place in that dreamlike liminal zone between cinema and theater, art and entertainment, character study and cautionary tale, farce and drama. It says less than it thinks, but it resonates more than you’d expect.
author: Alex Saveliev

quote: This is a movie that grabs you by the throat, then sticks in it.
author: Josh Larsen

quote: It has such lofty ambitions and go-for-broke performances, but never really connects.
author: Bill Goodykoontz

quote: Digger's satire may not change your thinking on global warming, but there are excellent performances and more than a few laughs.
author: Michael Calabro

quote: For all the film’s crazy performances, its directorial grandstanding, its wildly miscalculated rug-pulling, a genuine current of civilizational despair runs through Digger. That sadness, that horror, serves as Iñárritu’s ultimate justification, and this time, it’s a compelling one. Somewhere behind that camera, he acknowledges that he is just as lost as the rest of us.
author: Bilge Ebiri

quote: To paraphrase the great Kyle Cooke, “Digger” should be fun, but it’s not even funny, and the sweaty clumsiness of its punchlines and sight gags only serve to make the script’s galaxy-brained satire feel more like the stuff of an IMAX-sized JibJab cartoon.
author: David Ehrlich

quote: Audiences will debate whether the final takeaway is self-deprecating or self-congratulatory, but either way, it's so far up its own ass that it can't breathe.
author: Reuben Baron

quote: Ultimately, your mileage with Digger may vary based on how much you like Tom Cruise, and how much you enjoy contemplating his life and career as a movie star and film artist.
author: Matt Singer

quote: Digger chokes on its own ambitions, and very few of the picture’s participants emerge still breathing.
author: Robert Daniels

quote: It’s about inertia and abdication, not solutions, and while I don’t entirely love this strange comedy, I’m giddy that it’s lurched into existence.
author: Amy Nicholson

quote: It’s less about politics and more about the function of art in crisis, yet remains oddly toothless for a film so insistent it’s making some sort of pronouncement.
author: Hannah Strong

quote: There’s funny material and precision-focused comic performances in the mix here, but they’re contained within a movie already resigned to not having anything new to poke fun at.
author: Alistair Ryder

quote: Cruise is digging for that Oscar win with a performance well outside of his wheelhouse, but in terms of sheer cinematic entertainment, “Digger” is one dry well.
author: Katie Walsh

quote: To be as generous to Digger as possible, it feels like an Armando Iannucci rewrite away from being a masterpiece. But that distance is nonetheless as vast as a civilization-blitzing ice shelf.
author: Scott Tobias

quote: The time is right for a satire about climate change, but a satire should leave us a little uncomfortable, a little more thoughtful, a little bit changed. “Digger” just leaves us exhausted.
author: Moira Macdonald

quote: An unrecognizable, Oscar-ready Tom Cruise is eager to show what he’s got as a paunchy, preening, tantrum-throwing Texas oil powerbroker.  He’s got plenty. The movie not so much.
author: Peter Travers

quote: Iñárritu's reliance on a structural twist is evidence that the movie cannot stand on its own narrative or thematic merits. It is best avoided, except as a soporific.
author: James Berardinelli

quote: Digger lacks emotional depth, being much more interested in the showmanship of tricks and razzle-dazzle than character development. While Cruise puts on a good show, he’s walking around the loose threads of the script to get there.
author: Monica Castillo

quote: Cruise has mistaken Iñárritu as a trusted collaborator of great depth and dimensions, when the director is instead simply a man of heaving weight, immovable and unyielding.
author: Barry Hertz

quote: Where legendary film director Ernst Lubitsch was famous for his “touch,” Iñárritu’s aesthetic style is more akin to a Godzilla-sized stomp.
author: Alonso Duralde

quote: There is something glib and overblown here. This film finds itself in a postmodern hole. And what do you do when you’re in a hole?
author: Peter Bradshaw

quote: A tedious satire, slamming capitalistic greed, anti-environmental profiteering, rampant corruption, and horrid narcissism with all the bluntness of the shovel its protagonist reveres.
author: Nick Schager

quote: A blathering misfire.
author: Donald Clarke

quote: Here’s the real problem: “Digger” isn’t funny. It’s nervy, in your face, adventurous, and bizarro in a free-swinging, out-of-the-box way. And it feels like a comedy, since it’s fueled by the relentless overacting of a bad Coen brothers movie. But “Dr. Strangelove,” built around the genius of Peter Sellers, was brilliantly funny. “Digger” borrows the doomsday architecture of “Strangelove” but leaves out the slyness, replacing it with a lavishly overscaled spectacle of browbeating.
author: Owen Gleiberman

quote: Visually impressive, and Cruise gives his all. But Digger doesn’t have much going on beneath the surface. A disappointing waste of a superb team.
author: Olly Richards

quote: But when you’re watching a film that doesn’t really seem to work, which then voluntarily indulges the suggestion that its very existence might be completely pointless – well, then, why did any of us, filmmaker or audience, bother in the first place?
author: Clarisse Loughrey

quote: The director and Cruise, as well as the crew and supporting cast...have purposefully given us something messy, ungainly, clever to a fault, and designed to play like a shriek of rage and pain. It’s impossible to simply dismiss as a mistake, and equally impossible to declare that it works in almost any capacity.
author: David Fear

quote: The relative restraint and expressive specificity of Plemons’s performance — his character holds his gaze on other people a touch too long, and his smile seems backlit by madness — is a relief, given the rest of the cast’s cartoony turns. It’s a bummer to see actors like Goodman, Stuhlbarg and Riz Ahmed so badly handled.
author: Manohla Dargis

quote: Digger – while not irredeemably awful – is ultimately a big disappointment.
author: Lou Thomas

quote: So one can appreciate the attempt, even if at some point we wonder if we’re seeing a version of our director and co-writer every time this cynical, self-destructive superrich fool blurts out “I know what I’m doing,” when it’s obvious he doesn’t.
author: Roger Moore

quote: The script, though, is low-level, a satire that seems filtered through the poppy absurdity of Wes Anderson with a loose plot that can't seem to find its stride.
author: Kristen Lopez

quote: Iñárritu commits one of the greatest sins a director can commit: believing his film will always be smarter than its audience.
author: Sophia Ciminello

quote: Once again, a filmmaker tries very hard to impress upon all of us a daring story that plays with traditional expectations in the hopes of unearthing a more interesting analysis. And once again, his hand exposes very little that impresses on such a scale.
author: Josh Parham

quote: Maybe Cruise and Iñárritu are a perfect pairing. There is no denying their underlying skill, their ability to captivate the camera and create works that are superficially scintillating. Yet the end result is rendered inert by their own overbearing narcissism. In its attempt to be great art, Digger becomes neither great nor art.
author: Richard Whittaker

quote: Tom Cruise takes enormous risks playing the outlandish title character, and his daring portrait of avarice and ego is occasionally striking in its ferocity. But this ambitious misfire is consistently sabotaged by Iñárritu’s gratingly unsubtle comedic approach – not to mention his introduction of a meta twist that further alienates the audience.
author: Tim Grierson

quote: Digger, the eighth feature film from Alejandro G. Iñárritu, is pure, empty-headed trickery, a drab-looking gewgaw with a million moving parts and nothing to say, even if it desperately claws at profundity every minute.
author: Stephanie Zacharek

quote: Digger is a grandiose folly of a film, a failure on its own perhaps impossible-to-satisfy terms.
author: Dana Stevens

quote: Digger is what happens when you give the week’s worst Saturday Night Live sketch an inexplicably large budget and delusions of grandeur.
author: William Bibbiani

quote: His eighth feature is so meta that you watch in excruciating weariness as it disappears up its own ass and then realize to your dismay that there’s another eardrum-shattering hour left to endure.
author: David Rooney

quote: Say what you will about Tom Cruise but at least when he falls he does it in spectacular fashion. For here, in this garish, cloth-eared and sanctimonious dud, he produces the performance equivalent of riding a motorbike off a cliff minus a safety parachute and then crashing loudly at the bottom in a burst of corny expletives and cringeworthy poses.
author: Kevin Maher

quote: Digger is Alejandro González Iñárritu’s purported cri de coeur against our wealth-and-resources-hoovering overlords, but somehow it still manages to be a shameless Tom Cruise ego stroke.
author: Keith Uhlich

quote: Tom Cruise’s latest film, Digger — the actor’s first real stinker in nearly 10 years — really is a rage-inducing sit. Not because of the environmental issues it depicts in such a dated and obvious way, but due to a pair of enormous egos being blinded to their baby’s badness.
author: Johnny Oleksinski

quote: The mess isn’t even hot here; it’s as ice cold as the filmmakers think their satire is, and as devastatingly bad as the cataclysmic climate control crisis at the center of its plot.
author: Odie Henderson

quote: This movie is to funny what Exxon is to Greenpeace.
author: Kyle Smith
